H&P – Detailed

Consult Summary:
Adult with known eczema reports a 3-day worsening flare characterized by widespread red, sore, very itchy, dry patches over chest, arms, hands, and flexures; treated remotely with stronger topical steroid (Betnovate) and oral antihistamine (Fexofenadine) plus continued emollients, with follow-up in two weeks or sooner if symptoms worsen.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Worsening itchy, red, sore, dry skin rash.  
• Onset/duration: Began “past few days”; progressively worsening.  
• Distribution: Chest, hands, arms, especially antecubital fossae (worst area).  
• Character: Very pruritic; skin feels dry; some cracks present; no weeping or exudate noted; no thickened or lichenified areas; no visible scratch marks described.  
• Associated symptoms: Denies fever, temperature, joint pains, or systemic symptoms. Breathing remains normal.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: None specifically identified. Hydrocortisone cream and prior OTC antihistamine (cetirizine) provided no relief.  
• Review of systems (pertinent negatives): No fever, no joint pains, no respiratory compromise.  

Past Medical History:
• Atopic eczema – chronic, with previous flares; customarily managed with Diprobase emollient and Dermol wash; previously used OTC hydrocortisone.  
• Asthma – intermittent; uses blue (salbutamol) inhaler PRN; no recent exacerbations reported.  

Medications:
• Diprobase cream – topical emollient (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Dermol wash (patient states “dermal”) – topical emollient cleanser (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Hydrocortisone 1% OTC – topical corticosteroid (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Salbutamol “blue inhaler” PRN – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
New prescriptions today:  
• Fexofenadine – oral antihistamine (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Betnovate (betamethasone valerate) – topical corticosteroid, apply thin layer twice daily for 2 weeks.  

Allergies:
• No known drug allergies.

Social History:
• Lives in London; no additional social, smoking, alcohol, or substance use history documented.

Family History:
• Mother: Migraine, hypothyroidism.  
• No other family history reported.

Physical Examination:
• Not performed (telemedicine consultation). No vitals available.

Investigations:
• None ordered or reviewed during this encounter.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Extensive eczema flare
  • Assessment: Acute exacerbation of chronic atopic dermatitis involving chest, upper limbs, flexures; no signs of secondary infection.  
  • Plan:
    – Start Fexofenadine (oral antihistamine) to reduce pruritus.  
    – Start Betnovate topical steroid: apply fingertip unit twice daily for 2 weeks.  
    – Continue regular emollients (Diprobase cream, Dermol wash).  
    – Educate on thin-layer application and body-site coverage.  
    – Advise to monitor for adverse reactions (e.g., steroid-related skin changes, allergy).  
    – Follow-up: If worsening or no improvement within 2 weeks, or any adverse reaction, contact service earlier.

Issue 2: Asthma (stable)
  • Assessment: Intermittent, currently asymptomatic.  
  • Plan:
    – Continue PRN salbutamol inhaler.  
    – No change to current regimen.

General Plan items:
• Prescription sent electronically to Boots pharmacy for collection.  
• Safety-netting provided regarding worsening rash or systemic symptoms.

Quality checks:
● Missing but expected elements: vital signs; detailed physical examination; complete medication list with doses; smoking/alcohol history.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear dialogue; occasional minor overlaps but clinically adequate.
